subject: Pilot logistics & success metrics — next steps
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Tom Whitaker <tom.whitaker@nimbuslogistics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot logistics & success metrics — next steps

Hi Tom / Lena —

Thanks again for carving out time earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a shared checklist heading into the pilot kickoff: 

Summary of customer pain & goals
- High-level pain: manual routing exceptions and high latency in shipment ETA predictions during peak load windows (sporadic 3–7s tail latency).
- Business goal: reduce incorrect routing exceptions by 40% and average inference latency < 200ms for 75% of requests in the pilot dataset.

Scope (what we propose for the 4-week pilot)
- Data: 2 weeks of anonymized shipments + sample event stream (S3 presigned bucket).
- Workloads: batch re-score job (throughput focus) + low-latency API for real-time ETA corrections (p95 targets).
- Deliverables: baseline benchmark, prompt/eval set, paired A/B runs vs current model, final playbook for production rollout.

Success metrics (mutually agreed)
- Primary: 40% reduction in routing exceptions (measured on labeled holdout).
- Latency: p50/p95 token-level latency for inference; target p95 < 200ms for real-time endpoints.
- Cost proxy: tokens/second and per-request cost delta vs baseline.

Owners & points of contact
- Redwood PM (pilot owner): Marissa Cole — responsible for project schedule, eval harness, and delivery.
- Redwood Ops (infra & access): Grace O'Connor — network, VPC peering checklist, credentials.
- Nimbus technical lead: Tom Whitaker — will coordinate data export and internal stakeholders.

Immediate asks from Nimbus (items for this week)
1) Share a short export (S3 link or sample CSV) containing ~48 hours of events for baseline testing.
2) Confirm a read-only service account we can use or allow presigned S3 access.
3) Provide a contact for security/network to complete the access checklist.

Attachments: I attached a draft POC scope doc and a network access checklist (stubs below). Please review and flag anything missing.

Proposed timeline
- Week 0 (this week): access, data handoff, finalize success metrics.
- Week 1: baseline run + prompt/eval set creation.
- Week 2–3: iterative tuning, latency/cost profiling.
- Week 4: acceptance run + handoff playbook.

Next steps
- Tom: confirm access method (S3 service account or presigned URLs) by EOD Friday.
- Marissa & Grace: we will schedule a 30-min kickoff to go through the checklist and owners (can do early next week).

Thanks — I captured the above in the attached POC_Scope_v1.pdf. If that looks good I can post a calendar invite for next Tuesday.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.com

Attachment stubs:
- POC_Scope_v1.pdf (scope, metrics table, timeline)
- network_access_checklist.xlsx (IP ranges, firewall rules, role-permissions)
From: Tom Whitaker <tom.whitaker@nimbuslogistics.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Lena Morales <lena.morales@nimbuslogistics.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot logistics & success metrics — next steps

Thanks Sergio — good write-up, appreciate the clarity. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- Data: we can provide a 48–72 hour export in S3. Security prefers presigned URLs rather than creating new service accounts for short pilots. Is presigned acceptable?
- Timeline: we need to align Week 2 tuning windows with our low-volume windows (midnight–04:00 PT). Can Redwood run heavier batch jobs then?

Security questions (quick)
- Data retention: will Redwood persist copies of the dataset after the pilot ends? We prefer automatic purge after 30 days unless otherwise agreed.
- SOC2 evidence: our procurement needs an up-to-date SOC2 report and a point of contact for an evidence request.

Availability: I can confirm access by Friday if we provide the presigned link. For the kickoff meeting, earliest next week works for me Tue/Wed morning.

Tom
CTO, Nimbus Logistics
Tom.Whitaker@nimbuslogistics.com

Tom —
Appreciate the quick reply. Short answers + additions from our side: 

- Presigned URLs: totally fine for the pilot. Please include a sample schema file (CSV or Parquet) and a small README describing event columns.
- Retention: Redwood defaults to 30-day ephemeral storage for pilot datasets; we will auto-delete unless you ask us to hold for additional analysis. We will document that in the POC acceptance note.
- SOC2 / Security evidence: linking our security pack and SOC2 snapshot here for your procurement team to review: https://redwood-internal-secureshare.example/soc2-2026 and I'll introduce our security contact in the kickoff call.

Prompt/ev al plan note: We'll build a concise prompt set (20–30 prompts) focused on error classification and ETA correction tasks. For each prompt we'll capture pass/fail and confidence bins. If you have labeled examples for routing exceptions, please share 25–50 representative cases to speed up eval.

I'll put a 30-min kickoff on Tue Nov 2 at 09:30 PT (hold for now) — Sergio will add the access checklist and the POC scope as attachments.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Product Manager, Pilot Programs | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Marissa / Sergio —

Thanks for the clarifications. Confirming the following: 
1) We'll post a presigned S3 link to the sample export by EOD Thursday (includes README + schema + 48h events).
2) Retention: 30 days is acceptable. Please document purge policy in the kickoff notes.
3) SOC2: procurement will review the security pack; I'll loop in our procurement lead if they have follow-ups.
4) For labeled cases: sending 40 representative routing-exception examples in a separate secure email to Marissa.

Kickoff: Tue Nov 2 at 09:30 PT works for me — please send calendar invite and include the security and network owners. If possible, please attach the final POC scope to the invite.

One final ask before the kickoff: can Redwood share a brief list of the infra/network changes we should expect (eg inbound IPs, required ports, any IAM roles)? Grace, over to you to confirm the checklist fields we need Tom to complete.

Looking forward to it.
Tom
CTO, Nimbus Logistics
